written.myAnswer: A distance–time graph shows how the distance travelled by a body changes with time. A speed–time graph shows how the speed of a body changes with time.
Velocity is the gradient of the distance–time graph. Segment a: (2.0 km − 0 km)/(6 min − 0 min) = 20 km h⁻¹. Segment b: 0 km h⁻¹. Segment c: (0 km − 2.0 km)/(20 min − 10 min) = −12 km h⁻¹.

The gradient of a distance–time graph represents speed; the gradient of a speed–time graph represents acceleration. In each graph, gradient = change in vertical-axis quantity ÷ change in horizontal-axis quantity.

Distance–time graph:       S
                            │      /
                            │    /  gradient = speed
                            │  /
                            └──────── t

Speed–time graph:           v
                            │      /
                            │    /  gradient = acceleration
                            │  /
                            └──────── t
